# S05 — Build VM core memory and addressing modes

Implement the circular core of CORESIZE cells with modulo addressing, the cell type with its last-writer id, and operand evaluation for every addressing mode, test-first.

**Findings:** PROJECT.md Milestone 2 · **Size:** M · **Tree:** vm
Cites: C12 constraint: VM core is pure, C15 requirement: Spec covers and tests every opcode, modifier and addressing mode

**Not in this slice:** opcode execution, process queues, placement, scheduling, any I/O.

## Why

Milestone 2 (VM core with unit tests per opcode and addressing mode). Every other component reads and writes cells through this layer. The core must be pure (C12).

## Files

- VM core package source and unit tests (package path per the scaffolding layout).

## Failing tests

- One test per addressing mode, taken from the ISA spec's worked cases.
- Wraparound at address 0 and CORESIZE-1, and negative offsets.
- A write records the writing bot's id as last writer.
- A fresh core holds the spec's empty-cell value everywhere.

## Implement

- Pure module: no I/O, no clock, no RNG.
- Choose integer types so modulo arithmetic is exact and cannot overflow for any configured CORESIZE.
- Public read/write API that later slices use.

## Check

- The project test command passes.
- Each addressing mode in the spec has a named test.
- The VM core imports no I/O, time, thread or random APIs (under Rust: `rg -n 'std::(fs|io|net|time|thread|process)' <vm-core-dir>` prints nothing).
